chunks: That was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Abdullah ibn Khidash from Salih ibn Abdullah al-Khath'ami who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a truthful female slave-owner who claimed that she had breastfed one of my girls, should I believe her? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أُصَدِّقُهَا: Should I believe her / Is she believed
key_terms.أُمِّ وَلَدٍ: Female slave-owner who bore a child to her master

ai.seo_question: Is a woman's claim of breastfeeding her child sufficient to establish marriage prohibition in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) rules that a truthful woman’s claim of breastfeeding a child is not accepted as sufficient proof to establish the prohibition of marriage (radāʿ) on her own authority. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that while her testimony is credible, it does not carry the weight of a definitive legal ruling without corroborating evidence or an oath, distinguishing between mere testimony and established kinship. The context highlights the rigorous standards applied to *radāʿ* to prevent the unwarranted expansion of marital prohibitions.
